task:
You are working on an existing SwiftUI drawing assignment project.

Your task is to build PHASE 1 of a modular Iron Man Mark III engineering-sketch drawing system.

IMPORTANT:
This phase is ONLY architecture, layout, placeholders, and assembly sequencing.

DO NOT attempt to draw detailed Iron Man armor geometry yet.
DO NOT invent complex Paths.
DO NOT replace placeholders with finished armor.
Every visual armor component must initially be represented by a simple labeled rectangular bounding box.

The final goal is that I will manually replace each placeholder component, one Swift file at a time, with a custom SwiftUI Path later.

==================================================
CORE DESIGN GOAL
==================================================

Build Mark III as 74 independent visual SwiftUI components:

Helmet: 8
Torso: 20
Left Arm: 8
Right Arm: 8
Left Leg: 15
Right Leg: 15

Total: 74 independent armor component files.

Each component must live in its own Swift file.

The whole Mark III figure must be assembled from these files.

The project should support an animation where these 74 components appear one-by-one in sequence until the entire Mark III is assembled.

For now, every component is ONLY a rectangular placeholder showing:
- component number
- component short name
- approximate bounding area

The placeholder figure should already resemble a human / Iron Man silhouette in overall proportions.

==================================================
ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLES
==================================================

Strict separation of responsibilities:

1. Component file
Responsible only for local visual content.

Example:
LeftShoulderBell.swift

It should NOT know its absolute screen position.

2. Regional Assembly file
Responsible for placing related components.

Examples:
HelmetAssembly.swift
TorsoAssembly.swift
LeftArmAssembly.swift
RightArmAssembly.swift
LeftLegAssembly.swift
RightLegAssembly.swift

3. MarkIIIAssembly.swift
Responsible for combining all regional assemblies.

4. Animation / assembly state
Responsible for controlling which numbered components are currently visible.

Do not put independent @State variables inside all 74 component files.

Use one centralized assembly state / currentStep system.

5. Layout must scale responsively.

Do not hard-code the whole drawing around one specific iPhone screen.

Create a canonical drawing coordinate space and scale it into the available GeometryReader size while preserving aspect ratio.

==================================================
PLACEHOLDER DESIGN
==================================================

Create one reusable PartPlaceholder view.

Every one of the 74 component files should use it.

Example concept:

struct PartPlaceholder: View {
    let number: Int
    let name: String

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Rectangle()
                .stroke(...)

            Text(...)
        }
    }
}

Visual style:
- thin engineering-sketch-like stroke
- transparent fill
- small centered part number
- small short label
- low visual weight
- readable in debug mode
- no bright production colors
- preferably sepia / graphite tone

Each component file should remain extremely simple.

Example:

struct LeftShoulderBell: View {
    var body: some View {
        PartPlaceholder(
            number: 29,
            name: "L SHOULDER"
        )
    }
}

No absolute .position(...) inside this file.

==================================================
CANONICAL DRAWING SPACE
==================================================

Create a canonical coordinate system for the whole figure.

Recommended conceptual canvas:

width: 390
height: 760

or another similar portrait ratio.

The Mark III should be centered.

Use a GeometryReader outside the drawing and scale the canonical canvas uniformly so the result fits on:
- iPhone portrait
- iPad
- macOS SwiftUI preview/window

Preserve aspect ratio.

Do not independently scale X and Y.

==================================================
OVERALL BODY PROPORTION
==================================================

This is a frontal engineering-sketch blockout.

The silhouette should approximately follow:

- head centered
- shoulder width clearly wider than waist
- chest broad
- torso tapered slightly inward toward waist
- pelvis centered
- legs separated naturally
- arms hanging slightly away from torso
- hands near upper/mid thigh
- overall superhero proportions
- Mark III should feel athletic, not cartoonishly oversized
- approximately 7.5–8 heads tall

This does NOT need detailed armor accuracy yet.

The current goal is only correct bounding regions.

==================================================
REGIONAL ASSEMBLY RESPONSIBILITY
==================================================

HelmetAssembly.swift:
positions parts 01–08

TorsoAssembly.swift:
positions parts 09–28

LeftArmAssembly.swift:
positions parts 29–36

RightArmAssembly.swift:
positions parts 37–44

LeftLegAssembly.swift:
positions parts 45–59

RightLegAssembly.swift:
positions parts 60–74

Each regional assembly may use:
- .frame(...)
- .position(...)
- .offset(...)
- zIndex

The component files themselves must not.

==================================================
ASSEMBLY ORDER
==================================================

The default animation order should follow part numbers 1 through 74.

One part appears at a time.

Architecture must support:
currentStep = 0...74

A part should be visible if:

currentStep >= partNumber

Create a clean reusable mechanism for this.

Avoid copying 74 unrelated state variables.

==================================================
ANIMATION
==================================================

For Phase 1, animation should remain simple and structural.

Each newly appearing placeholder should:
- fade in
- start slightly offset from its final position
- settle into its final location

Direction can depend on body region:

Helmet:
slight downward entry

Left-side components:
slight left-to-right entry

Right-side components:
slight right-to-left entry

Torso:
slight scale / vertical settle

Legs:
slight upward entry

Do not create complicated animation yet.

Do not add particle effects.
Do not add glowing armor effects yet.

Use a subtle spring or easeInOut.

The architecture should make it easy to later replace placeholder animation with:
1. Path drawing animation
2. physical assembly / snap animation

==================================================
CONTROLS
==================================================

Create a minimal debug UI.

Required controls:

- Previous
- Next
- Reset
- Play All

Also display:

currentStep / 74

Example:
23 / 74

Play All should automatically progress through all 74 steps.

Use a reasonable delay such as 0.08–0.15 seconds per part.

Do not block the main thread.

The animation should be cancellable/resettable cleanly.

==================================================
DEBUG MODES
==================================================

Create a centralized debug/style configuration.

For example:

showBoundingBoxes
showLabels
showPartNumbers

During Phase 1 these should default to true.

Later I will disable them.

Do not embed separate debug constants across 74 files.

==================================================
Z-ORDER
==================================================

Set up reasonable z-ordering now.

General idea:

rear / inner armor
↓
larger structural plates
↓
front plates
↓
reactor
↓
face plate / hand plates where appropriate

Exact accuracy is not essential yet.

But avoid obvious overlap bugs.

==================================================
PAPER / BACKGROUND
==================================================

A very simple engineering-sketch background is allowed.

Keep it subtle.

For now:
- warm off-white / parchment-style background
- no image assets required
- no texture generation required
- no heavy visual effects

The focus is blockout.

==================================================
DO NOT DO THESE THINGS
==================================================

Do NOT:

- draw finished Mark III armor
- generate detailed Path geometry
- use image assets as the main armor
- make one giant MarkIIIShape
- put all 74 shapes into one Swift file
- use Canvas for the whole character
- put absolute coordinates inside individual component files
- duplicate 74 independent @State visibility variables
- create complicated glowing effects yet
- redesign unrelated parts of the project
- delete existing useful project code without reason

==================================================
IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY
==================================================

Follow this workflow strictly:

1. INSPECT
Inspect the current SwiftUI project and determine:
- existing app entry point
- current drawing views
- current architecture
- deployment target
- previews
- naming conflicts

2. EDIT
Add the new modular Mark III architecture.

3. VERIFY
Build the project.

Resolve compiler errors.

Verify:
- all 74 component files exist
- all component files compile
- all regional assemblies compile
- MarkIIIAssembly compiles
- currentStep 0–74 works
- Previous works
- Next works
- Reset works
- Play All works
- layout is visible on an iPhone preview
- figure remains centered and scaled

4. SYNTHESIZE
Report:
- files created
- files modified
- architecture summary
- whether build succeeded
- any remaining layout concerns
- exact next recommended component to manually draw first

==================================================
IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT PHILOSOPHY
==================================================

This is a blockout system similar to blocking out a 3D model before sculpting.

The rectangles are intentional.

Do not try to improve them into armor.

The user will manually replace each placeholder with a real SwiftUI Path one file at a time.

The most important success criteria for Phase 1 are:

1. clean modularity
2. correct overall human proportions
3. sensible part bounding boxes
4. stable responsive layout
5. clean assembly sequencing
6. easy future manual editing
7. build success

If uncertain between adding detail and preserving architecture,
choose architecture.

Proceed.
Additional constraint:

Before editing, create a concise implementation plan and explicitly map every part number 01–74 to:
- component Swift file
- owning regional assembly
- approximate frame size
- approximate canonical center position
- intended zIndex

Then implement from that map.

Do not improvise positions independently while creating files.

Treat this mapping as the single source of truth for the Phase 1 blockout.
